questions.a: 'from' — 'different than' is the classic error boards test. A wrong answer 'than' shows unlearned collocation.

questions.q: Fix: 'We discussed about the plan and then returned back home.'
questions.a: 'discussed the plan' and 'returned home' — both partners are redundant; discuss and return are complete. A wrong answer fixing only one shows partial redundancy-auditing.
'to' — 'married to' is the fixed partner; 'married with' is Hindi-transfer ('se shaadi'). Same family: 'angry with', 'pleased with', 'familiar with/to'.

What is Preposition collocation? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Preposition collocation is memorized territory: verbs, adjectives, and nouns each demand fixed partners — 'depend on', 'good at', 'afraid of', 'insist on', 'different from' (not 'than'), 'married to', 'listen to'.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Preposition collocation?
questions.a: Students translate Hindi postpositions into English prepositions — 'married with', 'angry on' — and add redundant partners to complete verbs ('discuss about', 'return back', 'repeat again').

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student supplies the fixed preposition for ~40 high-frequency collocations and corrects the board-favourite errors (different-than, discuss-about, comprise-of).
